full_judgment: 9. It appears that on receipt of the petition of complaint, the learned Magistrate took cognizance under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and also under section 406 of the Penal Code together after recording the initial statement of the complainant under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. At the time of hearing charge, the trial Court at first framed charge under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act by excluding another alleged offence under section 406 of the Penal Code. It may be mentioned here that Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 is a special law and the offence under the penal Code, cannot be tried jointly with the offence under the special law. Though initially cognizance was taken under both of these sections of 2 different categories of law on 14-6-2005, the offence under section 406 of the Penal Code was finally excluded in the right direction at the time framing charge of the first instance. When the order of framing charge under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act was challenged, the learned Sessions Judge correctly found that the charge under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act cannot be framed as the required legal notice could not be issued and served and case could not be filed within the stipulated period of limitation. So the order of framing charge under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act was set-aside and the accused-petitioner was discharged by the learned Sessions Judge by a contested judgment dated 28- 6-2007 passed in Criminal Revision No. 22 of 2006. The judgment appears to have been passed rightly and none of the parties challenged the same before the higher Court, Therefore, original CR Case No. 103 of 2005 stood disposed of conclusively by the said judgment and the trial Court had no scope reopen the said proceeding in any manner. But it appears from the record that the Chief Judicial Magistrate reopened the same proceeding by putting a new number as CR Case No. 3 of 2009 on the basis of an application of the complainant after a long time, and ultimately he framed charge under section 406 of the Penal Code by an order dated 4-2-2010, which was upheld by the learned Sessions Judge, Nilphamari by the impugned judgment and order dated 23-2- 2010 passed in Criminal Revision No. 21 of 2010.
